messages:
pagerduty: PagerDuty ALERT PD-4532 — redwood-runtime-prod — HIGH p95 latency > 700ms (3/3 checks). Triggered at 2026-05-11T14:02:47Z. https://pd.example/PD-4532 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Created incident thread for PD-4532 and attached alert details. Auto-channel: #eng-oncall. Related metric: latency_p95.
Emma: Acked. I'm oncall — looking now.
Emma: Quick glance at dashboard: sharp spike at 14:02:40, lasted ~45s, p95 hit ~820ms then dropped back. No sustained elevation.
Sanjay: I'm available — pulling logs and tailing the runtime pods. Any customer reports?
Emma: No customer Slack tickets so far. Sampling 50 requests across regions — only 2 had >700ms, both retried successfully. Estimated ~0.7% of requests in that 45s window.
Kai: grabbing kube logs. Seeing a burst of small GC/compaction messages on model-server-3. Also a couple of `grpc: timeout awaiting response` entries around 14:02:41.
Kai: Paste logs snippet:
```
model-server-3 | 14:02:40.987 INFO compaction: started
model-server-3 | 14:02:41.012 WARN grpc: request timed out id=0x7f9
model-server-3 | 14:02:41.200 INFO compaction: completed in 210ms
```
Sanjay: Looks like a short compaction/GC pause coincident with higher request queuing. Worker CPU hit 98% for ~30s on that node. No OOM.
ops-rotation-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4533 re-fired (same symptom) at 14:04:10 — escalated to Emma due to repeat within 2m.
Emma: Saw the second alert. Both are short blips, same node involved. I do not see error rates climbing. Rolling a quick remedial action: draining model-server-3 to move traffic, and pin pod to a different node to observe.
Emma: command run: `kubectl cordon node-17 && kubectl drain node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Sanjay: After drain, p95 back to normal within 20s. No more alerts so far.
incident-bot: PD-4532 auto-resolved at 14:06:07. PD-4533 auto-resolved at 14:06:25.
Lucy: Quick impact assessment: transient tail latency spike affecting an estimated 0.5–1% of requests for <60s per occurrence. No customer-visible errors, no retries exhausted seen in logs. Marking customer impact: none (informational).
Kai: Root-cause hypothesis: compaction/GC on model-server process caused brief CPU stall and increased queueing, surfacing as p95 latency. Possibly correlated with background checkpoint merge that started around same time.
Sanjay: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: increase alert suppression to ignore spikes <60s or require 2 of 3 longer-window checks. Also add a runbook step to cordon/drain affected node if repeated.
Emma: I'll open a follow-up ticket to tune the alert and add a scheduled review of the compaction cadence. Ticket: RW-ops-7842.
Lucy: Can someone add a small note in the incident log with timeline and the mitigation (drain + node pin) so oncall handoff looks clear?
Emma: Added timeline to RW-ops-7842 and left a link in #eng-oncall.
Sanjay: No further action from oncall for now. Leaving this thread to ops-rotation-bot to monitor for 2h.
ops-rotation-bot: Monitoring mode enabled for PD-4532 related symptoms for 2h. Will reopen if new pages occur. :white_check_mark:
Emma: Thanks team — closing thread.
